label: second token m after first token u/v/w
explanation: Fires only at step t=1 (second original token) when the input is m and the first token is u, v, or w. Magnitude is set by the first token: u gives the max (~0.36), v about 0.84x of max, w about 0.56x. Does not fire on m at any other position, on m after other first tokens, or in the delimiter/copy phases (including when m is re-input during copying). Independent of L.

issues: No refutation found. On test the predicate has P=R=F1=1.0 (1653/1653), mass recall 1.0 and correlation 0.976, and misses --split test shows 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.

Dev profile backs every factual claim: all 1713 activations are at t=1 (orig_idx 1), with 0 in the delimiter and copy phases. in_tok is m for 100% of the activation mass, and prev_tok/first_tok is u, v or w only. The firing rate is flat across L.
Magnitude ordering checks out. Mass share divided by count gives u 0.409/557, v 0.343/558 (0.84x of u) and w 0.248/598 (0.56x of u). This matches the explanation, and the maximum activation is 0.364.
Each first token on its own gives precision 1.0 (u: 557, v: 558, w: 598 predicted steps), so no subset of the predicate fires falsely.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
